Frameworks

The custom element works in every framework that renders HTML. The wrappers are thin: they create a controller on mount, pass changed props to set(), and destroy it on unmount.

Plain HTML#

<script type="module" src="https://kucukkanat.github.io/bots/dist/bots.js"></script>

<bot-avatar type="clover" state="working" size="96"></bot-avatar>

Vanilla JavaScript#

import { createBot } from '@kucukkanat/bots';

const bot = createBot(document.querySelector('#agent'), { type: 'droid', size: 96 });
bot.on('state', (e) => console.log('now', e.state));

React#

import { BotAvatar } from '@kucukkanat/bots/react';

export function Agent({ busy, onBot }) {
  return (
    <BotAvatar
      type="clover"
      size={64}
      state={busy ? 'thinking' : 'default'}
      onReady={onBot}                      // the controller, for say(), react(), lookAt()…
      onState={(e) => console.log(e.state)}
    />
  );
}

Every option is a prop. Event props: onPoke, onBlink, onJump, onLand, onState. Props are compared by value, so re-rendering with the same props costs nothing. className and style go on the host element.

Vue#

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue';
import { BotAvatar } from '@kucukkanat/bots/vue';

const busy = ref(false);
const onReady = (bot) => bot.say('Hi from Vue!');
</script>

<template>
  <BotAvatar type="cat" :size="64" :state="busy ? 'thinking' : 'default'" @ready="onReady" />
</template>

Options are props; the controller arrives with the ready event. You can also use <bot-avatar> directly; tell Vue it's a custom element with compilerOptions.isCustomElement = (tag) => tag === 'bot-avatar'.

Svelte#

<script>
  import { bot } from '@kucukkanat/bots/svelte';
  export let busy = false;
</script>

<div use:bot={{ type: 'clover', size: 64, state: busy ? 'thinking' : 'default' }}></div>

The action creates the avatar inside the node, calls set() when its parameters change and cleans up on destroy.

Server rendering#

Avatars draw on a canvas, so they only exist in the browser. Importing the module on the server is safe (nothing touches the DOM until an avatar is created), but create avatars in client-only code: useEffect, onMounted, onMount, or a client component in Next.js. Give the host a fixed width and height so nothing shifts when the avatar appears.

'use client';
import { BotAvatar } from '@kucukkanat/bots/react';
